Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.
1.

Learned A.G.A. submitted that notice of this bail application was given to victim on 19.4.2023, but
no one has entered appearance on her behalf.

2. Heard Sri Virendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri Shailendra Singh, learned
counsel for informant, Sri Sunil Kumar Srivastava, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

3. The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail
Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.528 of 2022, under Sections
363,366,376,506 I.P.C. and 3/4 Pocso Act, Police Station-Baldeo, District-Mathura after rejection
of his Bail Application vide order dated 3.3.2023 passed by learned Additional Sessions
Judge/Special Judge,POCSO Act, Mathura.

4.  In the present case, initially F.I.R. was lodged against three named persons including the Pintu @ Prithvi Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126536464/
1 applicant for an offence under Sections 363 and 366 I.P.C. F.I.R. was lodged by the father of victim,
a minor girl aged about 14 years on 26.12.2022 that all the accused persons enticed her daughter and kidnapped her on 25.12.2022 from lawful guardianship of her father.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that victim was traced after about 3 days and she gave her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

He further submits that in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., victim has named two accused persons, but exonerated one co-accused Karan that he has not committed an offence of rape, however, she made specific allegation of offence of rape against the applicant and co-accused i.e. his brother namely Rahul.
However, victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has made allegation of rape on all the three accused.

6. Learned counsel further submitted that on basis of evidence recorded during investigation,
charge-sheet was filed only against applicant and two other co-accused were exonerated and referred statement of witness Zakir Ali Khan that on the date of occurrence, victim was alone and nobody was with her and referred paragraph 17 of affidavit that reason for false implication of applicant was village partybandi.

7. Learned counsel for applicant lastly submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 7.1.2023,
there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail,
he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
8.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail application and submitted that victim is a minor girl aged about 14 years and she has made consistent allegation against applicant.
So far as other two co-accused are concerned, they have been exonerated on the basis of evidence collected during investigation.
9. Learned counsel for informant submitted that not only the statement of victim remained consistent against applicant, but statement of independent witnesses are parrot like statements.
10.LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

sentences.text: a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: In the present case, victim is a minor girl aged about 14 years and allegedly she was kidnapped from her father's lawful guardianship by all the accused persons.
However, during investigation, it appears that evidence could not be gathered against other two co-accused and charge-sheet was filed only against the applicant.

12. So far as allegation in regard to applicant is concerned, it remained consistent in the F.I.R. as well as statements of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. against the applicant and that he being prior acquainted with the victim, will try to influence her.
So far as other arguments are concerned, it will be subject matter of trial.
13. In these circumstances, I do not find it being a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
14. Accordingly, the bail application is rejected.

However, Trial Court is directed to take all endeavour to record the statement of the victim within a period of three months from today and thereafter the applicant will be at liberty to file a fresh bail application before learned Trial Court.
15. Registrar (Compliance) to take steps.
